chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who made it incumbent upon himself to walk to the House of Allah (the Sacred Kaaba), and all his slaves were free; when he went out with his aunt to Mecca, he did not hire a mount for her nor did he accompany her. He said: 'It is not sufficient; he must hire a mount for her and go out with her.'

key_terms.نَذْر: Vow or pledge to perform an act of worship

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one vows to walk to Mecca but leaves dependents behind?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the condition of 'walking' in a vow is interpreted not as a rigid physical constraint but as a commitment to the mode of travel relative to one's dependents. The Imam clarifies that leaving a female relative behind without transport or companionship violates the spirit of the vow, requiring the vow-maker to hire transport for her and accompany her to ensure her comfort and safety. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that vows are fulfilled through the completion of the intended benefit and care, rather than mere literal adherence to the method.
